messages.content: Help me create a queue with a myWorkerFunction that processes tasks, setting the concurrency level to 5 and without specifying a payload size?

function.name: queue_1
function.description: This function creates a queue object with a specified worker function and concurrency level. It allows for tasks to be added to the queue and processed according to the concurrency level. Optional payload size can be specified to limit the number of tasks processed per worker call. Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax.

worker.description: The worker function that processes each task. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

concurrency.description: The maximum number of tasks to be processed concurrently. This is JavaScript float type parameter in string representation.

payload.description: Optional. The number of tasks each worker function call should process at most. Default 0.0 This is JavaScript float type parameter in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to use the function queue_1 from the namespace functions. We need to pass worker as a string representation of the function. The user says "myWorkerFunction". So we need to provide a string representation of the worker function. They didn't give the actual code, so we can just put a placeholder like "function(task) { /* process task */ }" or maybe "myWorkerFunction". But the function expects a string representation of a JavaScript object. So we can pass "myWorkerFunction" if it's defined elsewhere. But better to provide a function body.

We also need concurrency: "5". No payload param.

So we call functions.queue_1 with arguments: worker: "function(task) { /* your processing logic here */ }", concurrency: "5".

We don't specify payload. That will default to 0.0.

Thus we produce a JSON object with the function name and arguments. According to the tool usage, we need to output a JSON object with the function name and arguments. The format: {"name":"queue_1","arguments":{...}}. Then the system will handle it.

Thus we output:

{
"name":"queue_1",
"arguments":{
"worker":"function(task) { /* your processing logic here */ }",
"concurrency":"5"
}
}

That's it.
